scheme_name: "Sugarcane Nursery Premium" Sub-Scheme of the "Crop Production Technology" Scheme
description:
The "Sugarcane Nursery Premium" Sub-Scheme is a component of the broader "Crop Production Technology" Scheme initiated by the Government of India.

This sub-scheme was launched in the year 2021 as part of the efforts to enhance sugarcane production in the country.

The primary objective of the Sugarcane Nursery Premium Sub-Scheme is to promote the establishment of quality sugarcane nurseries.

The scheme aims to increase the availability of quality planting material for sugarcane farmers.

By providing financial assistance for nursery establishment, the government seeks to enhance productivity and improve the income of sugarcane farmers.

The measurable target of the scheme is to establish at least 1 lakh nurseries across various sugarcane growing states by the end of 2025.

The scheme also aims to increase the average yield of sugarcane from 70 tons per hectare to 100 tons per hectare within five years.

Farmers participating in this scheme can receive a premium of up to INR 25,000 per hectare for establishing a sugarcane nursery.

This financial assistance is provided to cover the costs associated with the establishment of nurseries, including seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation.

The benefits of the Sugarcane Nursery Premium Sub-Scheme extend to small and marginal farmers who are primarily engaged in sugarcane cultivation.

Eligibility criteria for the scheme include farmers who own a minimum of 0.5 hectares of land dedicated to sugarcane cultivation.

Farmers must also be registered with the local agricultural department to qualify for the premium.

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years, ensuring that only adult farmers can apply.

Income criteria stipulate that the annual income of the farmer should not exceed INR 2 lakh to qualify for the scheme.

The application process for the Sugarcane Nursery Premium Sub-Scheme involves several steps.

Farmers must first obtain an application form from the local agricultural office or download it from the official government website.

The completed application form must be submitted along with required documents such as proof of land ownership and identity proof.

Farmers are also required to submit a detailed project report outlining the nursery establishment plan.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local agricultural officer for verification.

The approval process typically takes about 30 days from the date of application submission.

Upon approval, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account.

The disbursement is usually made in two installments.

The first installment is released upon approval of the application.

The second installment is released after the successful establishment of the nursery.

The timeline for nursery establishment is set at six months from the date of receiving the first installment.

The implementing authority for the Sugarcane Nursery Premium Sub-Scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

The scheme is executed through the respective state agricultural departments.

Farmers can contact the local agricultural office for assistance and guidance regarding the application process.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crores for the implementation of this sub-scheme over a five-year period.

This budget is aimed at supporting farmers and enhancing sugarcane production across the country.

The scheme is expected to benefit approximately 2 lakh farmers annually.

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme also provides technical support to farmers.

Farmers will receive training on best practices for nursery management and sugarcane cultivation.

The training sessions are conducted by agricultural experts and are designed to improve farmers' skills.

The government also plans to establish demonstration plots to showcase successful nursery establishment techniques.

These demonstration plots will serve as learning centers for farmers in the region.

The Sugarcane Nursery Premium Sub-Scheme is part of the government's larger initiative to boost agricultural productivity.

The initiative aligns with the National Policy for Farmers which aims to enhance farmers' income and ensure food security.

The scheme also contributes to the Sustainable Development Goals by promoting sustainable agricultural practices.

The government encourages the use of high-yielding and disease-resistant sugarcane varieties through this scheme.

Farmers are also encouraged to adopt modern farming techniques to improve productivity.

The scheme is expected to have a positive impact on the rural economy by increasing farmers' income.

Increased sugarcane production will also benefit the sugar industry and related sectors.

The government is committed to monitoring the progress of the scheme through regular assessments.

Feedback from farmers will be collected to improve the implementation of the scheme.

The Sugarcane Nursery Premium Sub-Scheme is a significant step towards enhancing the livelihoods of sugarcane farmers.

By providing financial and technical support, the government aims to create a sustainable sugarcane farming ecosystem.

The scheme also addresses the challenges faced by farmers in accessing quality planting material.

Through this initiative, the government seeks to ensure that farmers are equipped with the necessary resources to succeed.

Overall, the Sugarcane Nursery Premium Sub-Scheme represents a comprehensive approach to improving sugarcane cultivation in India.

It reflects the government's commitment to supporting farmers and enhancing agricultural productivity.

The scheme is expected to play a crucial role in transforming the sugarcane sector in the coming years.
